topic.title: "Please write it down": the bank manager's insurance pitch
topic.claim: We don't say no to the person behind the desk because we assume they know better, and the only thing that breaks the spell is asking for it in writing.
topic.behaviour: Customers visit a branch for something routine and get steered toward ULIPs or insurance. One user got out of it by asking for the requirement in writing with an employee ID. Others say every bank does this.
topic.mechanism: We fear looking foolish in front of an authority, and branch targets turn a service desk into a sales desk. Many of us stay quiet to avoid friction.
topic.group: salaried urban Indians who bank at branches, and their parents
real_details: A user says a manager refused to process a pre-approved loan document unless they bought a ₹45,000 ULIP-insurance combo
The user asked for the demand in writing on letterhead to take to the ombudsman and the manager backed off
The user then saw an elderly man being pitched an endowment plan with his fixed deposit
Commenters said nearly all banks do this and one self-described bank employee said staff are pushed by targets
Another commenter described hearing a manager give staff targets on speakerphone
topic.why_now: The thread went viral and is a reminder before festival-season bonuses and FDs get parked in branches.

score.best_hook: I went to the bank to renew an FD. Twenty minutes later I was being sold a ULIP I never asked for.

Then add one short, warm line in her voice about parents. A quoted 'arre, iski kya zaroorat thi' would add the Hindi texture the post currently lacks.

Cut it or turn it into a direct reader line, e.g. 'You went in for an FD. The desk had a target.' Also note the source frames the 20 Ulips as 'let us say' hypothetical, so keep 'example' and don't make it sound like a real count.

slide 2: 'says the user in a viral thread' and 'The price of that paperwork?' read like a news summary. Rewrite in Ananya's texting voice, e.g. 'He asked for the demand in writing, on letterhead, so he could take it to the ombudsman. The manager backed off.' Use 'the manager', since the source never gives his gender. Drop 'So they asked' because the user/he pronouns are inconsistent.

slide 3: 'Bank RMs say sales targets and incentives drive this' is the most reportorial line in the post. Make it sound like a person, and mark the 20 ULIPs as the RM's 'let's say' example, not a real quota. Add one line of Ananya inside the behaviour ('I'd nod too'), since she is meant to be inside it and nothing in the post shows that. 'Someone with a cabin' is a good line, so keep it.

slide 4: Change 'said banks push insurance' to past tense: 'said banks were pushing insurance on customers who didn't need it', to match the source. The mixer line is the best in the post, so let it breathe. Put the Sitharaman line on its own as a short punch, not as the third item in a stack.

slide 5: This is advice, which is manual territory, not a mirror. Also, 'auto driver' is a sudden jump out of the bank world. Either cut the auto comparison or tie it back to the branch. End on the feeling, e.g. why 'please write it down' works when 'no' feels rude. The 'isn't rude, it's the only no that works' structure is fine once, but 'the only no that works' overclaims from one thread, so soften it to something like 'the no that worked for him'.

slide 3: This is the flattest slide. 'Sales incentives are usually part of their pay' is a report line. Make it a feeling the reader knows, e.g. the person smiling across the desk is also counting their month's number. Keep the 20 ULIPs line as the hypothetical it is in the source ('let's say'), and don't present it as a real quota.

sources.fact: In February 2026, Finance Minister Sitharaman said banks were pushing insurance on customers who did not need it, and that mis-selling is punishable under the BNS.
sources.excerpt: a punishable offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). | focus on their core business instead of aggressively selling insurance products. | spending too much time pushing insurance even when customers did not need it. | unclear why they are being asked to 'de-risk' further by purchasing another insurance policy. | assumed insurance-related matters were overseen by the insurance regulator

sources.fact: Bank relationship managers say they try to sell insurance to customers who come in for routine products such as FDs, and sales targets and incentives drive this. One couple who came to renew FDs were offered a ULIP.
sources.excerpt: People come to our bank to invest in FD products and we try to sell them insurance plans. | Instead, they were offered a Ulip. | Bank RMs often market insurance products as high-return FDs. | Let us say, I have a target to sell 20 Ulips a month and my performance (metrics) is linked to that. | Incentives related to sales usually form a part of their salaries. | ask them why they are recommending it and how it will fit into your overall financial plan. | Review all documents carefully before signing on the dotted line.
